correctness.rationale: Put v_n=|cx_n| and z_n=sgn(cx_0)y_n off the fixed line. Then z_{n+1}=z_n+v_n and v_{n+1}=v_n(1+a/(1+z_n^2)). Thus v_n grows strictly, z_n>=z_0+n v_0 and the log of the product of multipliers is summable. Hence v_n tends to V>v_0, and z_n/n tends to V. The exact tail V-v_n=sum_{k>=n} a v_k/(1+z_k^2) first gives O(1/n), whence z_n=Vn+O(log n). The summand is then a/(V k^2)+O(log k/k^3), giving V-v_n=a/(Vn)+O(log n/n^2). The increments of z_n-Vn+(a/V)log n are summable with the required O(log n/n) tail. Undoing the two signed changes gives both stated coefficients even for negative x_0 or c. The fixed line is pointwise fixed; no off-line orbit is bounded or periodic. The combination at N,2N,4N cancels the affine terms and leaves +a log(2)/(cX). The packaged finite checks were inspected, not run, and are not needed for any quantifier.
residual_risks: Bounds here are orbit-dependent, not uniform in initial conditions or as a or c approach zero. No backward or forced dynamics are covered.
